plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 1: Structure and Bonding
plan.contextChunk: This figure renders a single methane molecule three ways in one row, moving from a solid-volume picture to a measured structural drawing to an open skeleton. At the left is a space-filling model in which four large off-white hydrogen spheres crowd around a dark gray carbon that is barely visible between them, the spheres touching and flattening against one another. In the center is a structural drawing: the central "C" joins an "H" directly above, an "H" at the left, and an "H" at the right by plain black lines, and a fourth "H" below by a heavy black wedge. A magenta double-headed curved arrow sweeps between two dashed magenta rays that extend the upward and left-hand bonds, labeled "Bond angle 109.5º". Short magenta dashed lines run rightward from the upper hydrogen and from the carbon to a vertical double arrow labeled "Bond length 109 pm". At the right is a ball-and-stick model with the dark gray carbon at the center and four pale hydrogen spheres held out on thin pale blue rods. Showing one molecule in three styles lets the reader attach the two measurements to a shape also seen as filled volume, fixing the tetrahedral geometry that results when four equivalent hybrid orbitals on carbon overlap with hydrogen orbitals.

authoredContext:
When each of the four identical sp3 hybrid orbitals of a carbon atom overlaps with the 1s orbital of a hydrogen atom, four identical C–H bonds are formed and methane results. Each C–H bond in methane has a strength of 439 kJ/mol (105 kcal/mol) and a length of 109 pm. Because the four bonds have a specific geometry, we also can define a property called the bond angle. The angle formed by each H–C–H is 109.5°, the so-called tetrahedral angle. Methane thus has the structure shown in the figure.

The structure of methane, showing its 109.5° bond angles.

The space-filling model, wedge-dash structure, and ball and stick model of methane. The bond length between C-H is 109 pm, and the bond angle of H-C-H is 109.5 degrees.
